before_results.readmission: Positive class: readmitted within 30 days of discharge. A missed readmission matters more because a patient the model doesn't flag goes home without extra follow-up and may relapse with worse conditions. A false alarm only costs an unneeded follow-up call or visit, although flagging too many patients could increase costs and stretch hospital staff.
before_results.diabetes: Positive class: has diabetes (doctor diagnosis or HbA1c ≥ 6.5%). A missed positive matters more because that person goes undiagnosed and untreated, with a higher chance of damage to the eyes, kidneys, nerves and heart. A false alarm only costs one extra follow-up blood test, a needle prick and some worry.
